paper.title: Design principles of deep translationally-symmetric neural quantum states for frustrated magnets
paper.authors: Rajah P. Nutakki, Ahmedeo Shokry, Filippo Vicentini

results.system_description: J₁–J₂ Heisenberg, 10 × 10 · J₂/J₁ = 0.5 · periodic · Sz = 0. H = J1 sum_<ij> S_i · S_j + J2 sum_<<ij>> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J1 = 1; J2 = 0.5; no constant shift
results.variant: translationally symmetric deep CNN (ConvNext blocks), L = 10
results.source_location: Table "Benchmark variational energies for the Shastry-Sutherland and J1-J2 models" (tab:benchmark), row J1-J2 (J1 = 1, J2 = 0.5), network ConvNext
results.eligibility_evidence: Variational energy per site of the optimized ConvNext state, with the Monte Carlo error of the final evaluation in parentheses (caption of the design-summary figure); the fViT and ResNet rows of the table are quoted.
results.notes: Spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2 (Eq. 1), L x L square lattice with periodic boundaries (Sec. 2). The number of parameters is printed as 2.6 x 10^5. The magnetization sector is not stated.

results.system_description: Shastry–Sutherland, 10 × 10 · J/J′ = 0.8 · periodic · Sz = 0. H = J sum_<ij> S_i · S_j + J' sum_dimers S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J' = 1; J = 0.8; no constant shift
results.variant: translationally symmetric deep CNN (ConvNext blocks), L = 10
results.source_location: Table "Benchmark variational energies for the Shastry-Sutherland and J1-J2 models" (tab:benchmark), row Shastry-Sutherland (J1 = 0.8, J2 = 1), network ConvNext
results.eligibility_evidence: Variational energy per site of the optimized ConvNext state, with the Monte Carlo error of the final evaluation in parentheses (caption of the design-summary figure); the fViT and ResNet rows of the table are quoted.
results.notes: Spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2 (Eq. 1), L x L square lattice with periodic boundaries (Sec. 2). The number of parameters is printed as 2.6 x 10^5. The magnetization sector is not stated. The table gives the couplings as J1 = 0.8 (nearest neighbors) and J2 = 1 (dimers), i.e. J/J' = 0.8 in units of J', while the text of Sec. 2 says J1 = 1, J2 = 0.8. The table's convention is the one of the instance: the same table compares with the factored ViT of Viteritti et al., -0.449329(1), which is their L = 10 energy at J/J' = 0.8 in units of J' (arXiv:2311.16889), and the two energies agree to 1.3 x 10^-5. The dimer pattern is that of Fig. 1.
